uncited: Dynamic and Spacetime Modeling extends static 3D Gaussian Splatting to handle temporal variations, enabling real-time novel view synthesis for dynamic scenes .
It solves the problem of modeling emerging, vanishing, and deforming content by integrating time-dependent attributes (motion, opacity, rotation) into the Gaussian representation .
It is distinguished from static methods by its explicit handling of time as a dimension, using either learned deformation fields or parametric polynomial trajectories to model geometry changes .
**Time Input:** All methods accept a time parameter $t$ to query the scene state .
**Optimization:** Training uses the Adam optimizer and minimizes a combination of L1 loss and D-SSIM loss between rendered and ground-truth images .
**Density Control:** Methods employ adaptive density control (densification, splitting, pruning) based on positional gradients and opacity thresholds to maintain representation quality .
**Initialization:** Gaussians are typically initialized from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) sparse point clouds .
